name: Babylon (First Dynasty)
description: Amorite kingdom on the Euphrates around Babylon, Sippar, Kish and Borsippa that Hammurabi turned into an empire.
status1792: Mid-sized kingdom (~ Sippar to Dilbat, roughly 100 x 60 km), junior ally of Shamshi-Adad and wary neighbour of Larsa and Eshnunna.
status1750: Empire of southern and central Mesopotamia from the Gulf to Mari and the Diyala; overlord of Ekallatum and much of the north.

name: Larsa
description: Kingdom of the far south, the dominant power of Sumer after Rim-Sin conquered Uruk (1802) and Isin (1794).
status1792: Largest state in the south: Larsa, Ur, Uruk, Isin, Nippur, Mashkan-shapir, Lagash.
status1750: Gone: conquered by Hammurabi in 1763; Rim-Sin taken prisoner. A Rim-Sin II revolted briefly under Samsu-iluna (1739).

name: Eshnunna
description: Diyala kingdom controlling routes to the Zagros and Elam; produced the Laws of Eshnunna.
status1792: Strong regional power expanding up the Tigris and Euphrates (it had held Rapiqum and Ekallatum's neighbourhood).
status1750: Annexed by Babylon (defeated 1762, city devastated c. 1756).

name: Mari
description: Middle Euphrates kingdom of Mari, Terqa and Tuttul; its palace archive is our main window on the age.
status1792: Province of Shamshi-Adad's kingdom, ruled by his son Yasmah-Addu.
status1750: Destroyed by Hammurabi (1761/1759); region later becomes the kingdom of Hana centred on Terqa.

name: Upper Mesopotamia / Ekallatum (Assyria)
ruler: Shamshi-Adad I (d. c. 1776), then Ishme-Dagan I
description: Shamshi-Adad's 'Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia' from the Zagros to the Euphrates, with capitals at Shubat-Enlil, Ekallatum (Ishme-Dagan) and Mari (Yasmah-Addu); includes Assur.
status1792: At its height: the strongest state in Mesopotamia.
status1750: Collapsed after 1776; Ishme-Dagan holds a rump around Ekallatum and Assur as a Babylonian client.

name: Elam (sukkalmah dynasty)
description: Iranian power with lowland capital at Susa and highland base at Anshan; recognised as overlord by Mesopotamian kings until 1765.
status1792: Distant senior power; arbiter of Mesopotamian disputes.
status1750: Driven back to Susiana after the failed invasion of 1766-1764; independent.

name: Yamhad
ruler: Yarim-Lim I (c. 1780-1764), then Hammurabi I of Yamhad
description: Kingdom of Aleppo, the greatest power of northern Syria.
status1792: Rising under Sumu-epuh, in conflict with Shamshi-Adad and Qatna.
status1750: Independent and powerful; dominant in Syria.

name: Qatna
description: Western Syrian kingdom, rival of Yamhad, allied to Shamshi-Adad.

name: Malgium
description: Small Tigris kingdom between Eshnunna and Larsa.

name: Der
description: Gate-kingdom on the road to Elam at the Zagros foot.

name: Apum (Shubat-Enlil)
description: Khabur-triangle kingdom based in Shamshi-Adad's former capital, one of many small 'Ida-Maras' and Habur kingdoms.
status1750: Small independent kingdom (later sacked by Samsu-iluna, 1728).

name: Zagros & Hurrian highland polities
ruler: Kuwari of Utûm; Turukkean and Gutian chiefs
description: Highland principalities east of the Tigris (Utûm, Qabra, Turukku, Gutium) fought over by Shamshi-Adad, Eshnunna, Elam and Babylon.
status1792: Independent; soon targeted by Shamshi-Adad's Qabra campaign (c. 1781).
status1750: Raided by Hammurabi (years 37 and 39) but not durably controlled.

name: Minor / uncertain polities
description: Small kingdoms (Karana, Kurda, Andarig, Ida-Maras) or places whose allegiance at a given date is uncertain.
